podcast.title: Phantom of the Paradise Fictional Band (1974)
podcast.body: The Undead is a made-up band featured in a scene within 'Swan's Rock Opera' in the 1974 film 'Phantom of the Paradise,' depicted during the construction of a Frankenstein-like monster named Beef. "The entire scene of the movie features a made up band called the Undead."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Phantom of the Paradise Fictional Band (1974)
podcast.body: The Undead is a made-up band featured in the 1974 film "Phantom of the Paradise" during the sequence depicting the construction of the Frankenstein-like monster Beef. The band members, especially the singer Peter Ebling, are depicted wearing corpse paint similar to that seen in modern death metal or black metal, leading to the theory that they represent a proto-goth or proto-death metal group from 1974.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Proto-Goth/Death Metal Visuals
podcast.body: The Undead, a fictional band from the 1974 film 'Phantom of the Paradise,' featured its singer, Peter Ibling, and the rest of the band made up in "corpse paint," a visual style compared to modern death metal or black metal, suggesting proto-goth or proto-death metal aesthetics. "The singer of the Undead is a dude named Peter Ebling. He is made up in corpse paint, and I like what you would see with modern death metal or black metal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Corpse Paint Aesthetics (1974)
xref.body: As the singer of the fictional band The Undead in the 1974 film 'Phantom of the Paradise,' Peter Ibling was depicted in "corpse paint," a visual style noted for its resemblance to modern death metal or black metal makeup, which contributes to the theory of the film being proto-goth or proto-death metal. "The singer of the Undead is a dude named Peter Ebling. He is made up in corpse paint, and I like what you would see with modern death metal or black metal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Corpse Paint in Phantom of the Paradise (1974)
xref.body: Peter Ebling, the singer of the fictional band The Undead in the 1974 film "Phantom of the Paradise," is depicted wearing corpse paint similar to what would later be seen in modern death metal or black metal. This early use of corpse paint contributes to the theory that the film contained elements of proto-goth or proto-death metal.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Potential Proto-Goth/Death Metal Inventor (1974)
xref.body: Paul Williams' work in "Phantom of the Paradise" in 1974, particularly the "Rock Opera" within the film and the fictional band The Undead (whose singer, Peter Ebling, wore corpse paint similar to modern death/black metal), leads to a theory that he accidentally invented proto-goth or proto-death metal music. Goth music didn't widely emerge until bands like Bauhaus in the late 1970s, and death metal in the mid-1980s.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
